title: Redis Cluster Sharding and Failover
summary: Keys map to 16384 hash slots spread across masters; clients follow redirections and topology updates, and replicas promote on failure.

nodes.label: Cluster-aware Client
nodes.detail: Caches the slot map and sends commands straight to the owning master. Refreshes topology on MOVED errors.

nodes.label: Hash Slots
nodes.detail: Each key maps to one of 16384 slots, and each slot belongs to exactly one master.

nodes.label: Master 1
nodes.detail: Serves reads and writes for its slots and replicates writes asynchronously to its replica.

nodes.label: Replica 1
nodes.detail: Follows master 1 and can be promoted if the master fails.

nodes.label: Master 2
nodes.detail: Owns the second slot range with its own replica.

nodes.label: Master 3
nodes.detail: Owns the third slot range with its own replica.

nodes.label: Cluster Bus
nodes.detail: Nodes exchange state over a separate port. When a majority of masters mark a node failed, its replica is promoted.

steps.title: Client hashes the key
steps.text: The client computes CRC16 of the key modulo 16384 to find its slot.

steps.title: Command goes to the owner
steps.text: Using its cached slot map, the command goes straight to the master that owns the slot.

steps.title: Writes replicate
steps.text: Each master streams writes asynchronously to its replica.

steps.title: Failure is detected
steps.text: Nodes gossip over the cluster bus; a majority marks an unreachable master as failed.

steps.title: Replica is promoted
steps.text: The replica takes over the slots; clients receive MOVED redirects and refresh their topology.
